**8. @0xSurferX**  
🚨 Sandbox your AI agent before it drains your wallet  
You gave an AI agent access to your bot.  
It can read your data, run your code AND touch your live wallet.  
You just handed the least unpredictable thing in your stack the keys to your money.  
Here's the box you put it in first:  
I've told you a hundred times: AI on the plumbing, NEVER on the bet.  
But more people are running actual agents now, ones that don't just write code, they DO things.  
And an agent is non-deterministic by nature.  
Same situation, different action, and no guarantee it does the safe thing every time.  
So the question stops being "is my agent smart."  
It becomes "what's the worst thing it can do if it goes wrong at 3am while i'm asleep."  
If the answer is "empty my wallet," you built a bomb.  
The fix is isolation.  
And this is what made my bot print after hundreds of failed attemps.  
Proof: [https://t.co/ZrYkEEFeTk]  
You run the agent in a locked sandbox where it physically CANNOT reach the dangerous stuff.  
> The agent runs in its own contained box, not on the same machine as your live keys.  
> It can read data, draft logic, propose actions - all the plumbing work.  
> It cannot sign a transaction, touch your wallet, or fire a real order directly.  
> Anything that moves money passes through a hard gate OUTSIDE the sandbox that you control.  
New runtimes are being built specifically for this, isolating unpredictable agent workloads so a misbehaving agent can't reach past its walls.  
That's the shape you want.  
Think of it like the kill switch, but structural.  
A kill switch stops a bad bot after it starts losing.  
A sandbox stops a bad agent from ever being able to do the damage in the first place.  
Both come from the same rule.  
> The thing that touches real money must be deterministic and gated.  
> The unpredictable thing lives in a box and hands its work OUT to that gate, never around it.  
An agent you can't contain is an agent you can't trust with a wallet.  
Let the agent think inside the box.  
Keep the trade button outside it, in your hands.  
Next post i break down the exact gate i put between an agent and a live order.
